package_info.package_versions: All versions of the rogue app as distributed
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is malicious because it impersonates a legitimate brand to deceive users, steal credentials, deploy additional malware, abuse in-app purchases, and exfiltrate sensitive data, resulting in financial loss and reputational damage. The app's behaviors include credential harvesting, unauthorized billing, malware delivery, and excessive permission requests, all of which are designed to exploit users and compromise device security.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user interacts with the login screen, the code collects the entered username and password, transmits these credentials to an attacker-controlled server over the network, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive user credentials and sends them to an unauthorized external server, which is a clear indicator of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should authenticate users by securely transmitting credentials to the official backend service, not to unknown or hardcoded domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may collect credentials for authentication, but only transmit them to trusted, official endpoints using secure protocols.
key_indicators: Credentials sent to non-official or hardcoded external domains
Absence of legitimate backend authentication logic
Presence of obfuscated or hardcoded attacker server URLs in code

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after free trial period or in-app purchase event)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the free trial period ends or an in-app purchase event occurs, the code initiates a subscription with an excessive fee and hides the subscription management UI, resulting in unauthorized or deceptive billing and making cancellation difficult.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exploits legitimate billing APIs to charge users excessive fees and deliberately obscures or removes subscription management options, making it difficult for users to cancel.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps must clearly disclose all fees and provide accessible, transparent subscription management controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Subscription management is legitimate when fees are reasonable and users can easily manage or cancel subscriptions; hiding controls and charging exorbitant fees is not.
key_indicators: Initiation of subscriptions with excessive or hidden fees
Obfuscated, missing, or disabled subscription cancellation UI elements
Automatic billing after free trial without explicit user consent

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user interaction with pop-up or ad)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user clicks on a pop-up or advertisement, the code downloads an additional APK from a non-official source and initiates its installation, resulting in the delivery and installation of further malware onto the device.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code entices users to install additional APKs from untrusted sources, a common method for delivering secondary malware payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should never prompt users to install unrelated or unsigned APKs, especially from non-official sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: App updates or plugins may be delivered, but only from official sources, with user consent, and through secure channels.
key_indicators: Pop-ups or ads prompting installation of APKs
Downloads initiated from non-official or suspicious sources
Requests for install_packages permission outside of legitimate update flows

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time or first launch, the app requests access to sensitive permissions such as contacts, external storage, and account information, enabling the collection and potential exfiltration of user data unrelated to the app's stated purpose.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app requests broad and sensitive permissions that are not justified by its described functionality, increasing the risk of unauthorized data access and exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should only request permissions necessary for their core features and must provide clear justification to users.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some apps may require access to contacts or storage for core features, but only with clear user benefit, consent, and transparent explanation.
key_indicators: Requests for sensitive permissions (contacts, storage, accounts) without clear user benefit
Permission requests at install-time for features not described in app documentation
Lack of in-app explanation or justification for requested permissions

attack_chain.action: User discovers and installs the rogue app from an app store or APK site.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is installed and can execute malicious behaviors.

attack_chain.action: App requests excessive permissions during installation or first launch.
attack_chain.leads_to: App gains access to sensitive data and device features.

attack_chain.action: App presents a fake login screen to harvest user credentials.
App initiates hidden or exorbitant in-app purchases after a free trial.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is charged excessive fees without clear consent.

attack_chain.action: App displays pop-ups or ads prompting user to install additional malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device is further compromised with additional malware.

behavioral_signatures: App requests permissions unrelated to its stated functionality or user benefit
Credentials are transmitted to non-official or hardcoded external servers
Initiation of in-app purchases with hidden or excessive fees and obscured cancellation options
Pop-ups or ads prompt installation of additional APKs or software from non-official sources
file_indicators: AndroidManifest.xml or Info.plist containing requests for sensitive permissions (contacts, storage, accounts) not justified by app description
Presence of hardcoded URLs or domains in code that are not associated with the legitimate brand
Obfuscated, missing, or disabled subscription management UI elements in app resources
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains or IPs not associated with the legitimate brand, especially those hardcoded in the app
Unencrypted transmission of user credentials over the network
Downloads of APKs or executables from non-official or suspicious sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor app stores and APK distribution sites for apps using your brand name or assets. Analyze app permissions for excessive or unrelated requests at install-time and runtime. Inspect network traffic for credential exfiltration or outbound connections to suspicious or hardcoded domains. Review in-app purchase flows for hidden or excessive fees and check for missing or obfuscated subscription management UI. Use static and dynamic analysis tools to identify hardcoded attacker infrastructure, obfuscated code, and unauthorized APK download/install behaviors.
